gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Koolatron's thermoelectric coolers (like its wheeled 33-qt pick) have no thermostat and always run at full cold, drawing about 4.5 A / 54 W at 12 V, and have no built-in low-voltage cutoff, so Koolatron sells a separate battery saver that switches off at 11 V, and that some vehicles cut power to the 12 V socket when the ignition is off.
standout_why: I compared GearJunkie (rank 1), Gift Sitter (rank 2) and lovethe88 wheels (rank 5). All three already give the 'about 36–40°F below ambient' limit for thermoelectric coolers, so that part is not new. GearJunkie warns in general that electric coolers can drain a car battery. Gift Sitter and lovethe88 mention 'three-level battery protection' on compressor models but give no cutoff voltages. None of the three says that thermoelectric units run nonstop with no thermostat and no cutoff, gives their amp draw, or mentions that some cars switch off 12 V socket power with the ignition off.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's advice to pick a compressor model and adds the reason that decides it. The Koolatron is the only thermoelectric option on its list. It runs flat out with nothing to stop it from draining the car's starting battery once the engine is off, and it may simply stop when the ignition cuts the socket. For a cooler that will sit in the car with the engine off, or be rolled away from it, the safer setup is a compressor cooler with its own battery. The Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L, which Dealectric lists, has a 288 Wh removable battery rated by Anker for 52 h on one battery in Eco mode, empty, at 77°F, and 6-inch wheels. Pages describing EverFrost 2 manuals mention three car-battery protection levels, but I could not open a source that gives their voltages.

findings.product: Koolatron thermoelectric coolers (P, D and W series, including W65 wheeled 31 L)
findings.label: Thermostat / duty cycle
findings.value: No adjustable thermostat; runs at maximum cold all the time
findings.source_title: 12V Cooler FAQs and Troubleshooting Guide | Koolatron
findings.note: Koolatron's wording: standard units 'do not have an adjustable thermostat and run at maximum cold.' Thermostat models are special order only, for medical and industrial use.

findings.product: Koolatron thermoelectric coolers (P, D and W series, including W65 wheeled 31 L)
findings.label: Current draw at 12 V
findings.value: 4.5 A (54 W); the smallest model, the P9, draws 3 A (36 W)
findings.source_title: 12V Cooler FAQs and Troubleshooting Guide | Koolatron
findings.note: Koolatron's wording: 'Most Koolatron thermoelectric coolers consume 4.5 amps or 54 watts of power at 12 volts.' My arithmetic: because the unit never cycles off, 8 hours with the engine off draws about 4.5 A × 8 h = 36 Ah from the car battery. A search snippet gave the W65 cord rating as 5 A / 60 W, but I could not open the W65 page (HTTP 429), so I have not used that figure.

findings.label: Low-voltage protection
findings.value: Not built in; Koolatron sells a separate battery saver that cuts off below 11 V
findings.source_title: 12V Cooler FAQs and Troubleshooting Guide | Koolatron
findings.note: The battery saver 'automatically switches the cooler off if the battery drops below 11 volts' and turns it back on when the engine restarts. On running from the battery with the vehicle off, the FAQ says only 'We recommend using your judgment and erring on the side of caution' and recommends the saver for longer periods.

findings.label: 12 V socket with ignition off
findings.value: Some vehicles have no power at the 12 V socket when the ignition is off
findings.source_title: 12V Cooler FAQs and Troubleshooting Guide | Koolatron
findings.note: From Koolatron's Troubleshooting Guide: 'Some vehicles do not have power to their 12V plugs when the ignition is off.' So on those cars, a cooler with no battery of its own stops cooling when the car is parked.

findings.product: Koolatron thermoelectric coolers (P, D and W series)
findings.label: Cooling limit
findings.source_title: 12V Cooler FAQs and Troubleshooting Guide | Koolatron
findings.note: Gift Sitter and GearJunkie already give this, so it is not part of the gap. Example of my arithmetic: in a 95°F car the best case is about 55°F inside, which is above refrigerator temperature.

findings.label: Own-battery runtime
findings.value: 52 h on one 288 Wh battery; 4.3 days on two batteries
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L Electric Cooler | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Anker's footnote for the 4.3-day figure: cooler empty, Eco mode, 2 fully charged batteries, 77°F ambient. Running on its own LFP battery means it does not need the car's 12 V socket while parked. The car-socket cable recharges the battery.

findings.label: Temperature range / wheels
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L Electric Cooler | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Compressor cooler, so its range is a fixed setting rather than an offset below ambient. The page showed no price when I read it.
